answer: Datagram cadence fingerprinting. Each identity must exhibit a mesa-like traffic shape: long flat inter-arrival plateaus broken by short bursts, matched against a falcon template the validator learns per agent. A prism check splits the timing histogram across three random epochs, and any identity whose plateau variance collapses (as scripted sybils do) is deprioritized until it re-earns queue slots. An attacker must run real workloads long enough to fill each plateau, costing roughly hours of compute and bandwidth per identity per epoch.
